about: Numbers for web/proof.html, computed by tools/make_proof.mjs from the app pipeline (data.js) on cached SPHEREx cutouts. AI-written code (Claude, Anthropic) for team Proper Motion, NASA Space Apps 2026.

settings.flagFilter: viewer default: no flag boxes ticked, no images hidden

motion: the measured speed is within 2 uncertainties (2σ) of the catalogue, and the uncertainty is no more than half the value.
between 2σ and 3σ, or the uncertainty is larger than half the value.
more than 3σ from the catalogue. Shown as measured, with the likely reason.

the catalogue motion is below 0.7″ a year (the smallest motion we call real, at least 3 × the 0.15″/yr floor), so it is too small to measure reliably in these images, the star's centre is blanked (masked pixels within 2 pixels of it) in 90% or more of the fitted images (the 90% limit), or the fit could not run. A saturation flag alone does not count; only a blanked centre does.
direction: measured and catalogue motions, compared as arrows (east and north parts together), are within 2σ. The two-part difference √((Δe/σe)² + (Δn/σn)²) is turned into the one-part σ with the same chance of happening by accident (2 degrees of freedom), so 2σ here means about 2.49 before the conversion and 3σ about 3.44.
more than 3σ: the arrow points measurably away from the catalogue's, even if the speed agrees. Shown with the likely reason.
brightness: the catalogue calls it a variable star, and we see its brightness change by more than 3σ between the first and last season, in at least one of the two wavelength groups.
the change is under 3σ: no clear change above the noise.
too few images where the star's centre is unmasked and the wavelengths match.

measured.floorText: floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 1 usable here)

tests.limit: The star carries the archive's saturation flag in 120 of 120 images, and its centre is blanked in 81 of the 120 fitted images, so its centre is found from the unsaturated edge pixels; images with a blanked centre count for less in the fit because their positions scatter more. The long-wavelength detectors alone give 10.52 ± 0.28″/yr, the short ones 9.40 ± 0.82″/yr. The speed agrees, but the direction is 5.7° off (349.9° measured, 355.6° catalogue): about 1.0″/yr sideways, 3.1σ. Likely because the star carries the saturation flag in 120 of 120 images and its centre is blanked in 81 of the 120 fitted, so the position comes from the star's edges, which can lean to one side; the 0.15″/yr floor comes from faint field stars and does not cover that. It stays off with the long-wavelength detectors alone (348.9°) and with every flagged image hidden (349.4°), so it is systematic, not noise.

measured.floorText: floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 1 usable here)

tests.limit: Epsilon Indi A is 6.7′ away, outside this 2.6′ patch, and no image has scattered-light flags near B; hiding every flagged image gives 4.35 ± 0.16″/yr. The value is 5% below the catalogue (1.4σ). Its error bar has a floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 1 usable here). Epsilon Indi B is itself a pair of brown dwarfs 0.7″ apart; their orbit moves the light centre by up to about 0.1″/yr, by different amounts at Gaia's visible wavelengths and SPHEREx's infrared ones, so a small difference is expected.

expected.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, Spitzer + WISE (via SIMBAD)

measured.floorText: floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 0 usable here)

tests.limit: Faint at short wavelengths: only the two longest bands (detectors 5–6, 3.8–5.0 µm) were used. With detectors 1–4 the fit gives 0.48 ± 0.44″/yr, because it locks on a background star (Gaia G 16.31) 7.8″ away that does not move. That background star (7.8″ away, inside the measuring circle at every wavelength) also blends with it in the long bands; its steady light likely pulls the measured speed low (6.53 vs 8.15″/yr), so this value is a lower estimate. For information: fitting that star out (a two-source fit with its Gaia position fixed and the star width measured on Epsilon Indi B) gives 9.04 ± 0.86″/yr from 25 images, +1σ from the catalogue; the verdict uses the standard method above.

measured.floorText: floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 2 usable here)

tests.limit: The catalogue motion (0.02″/yr) moves it only 0.022″ (0.004 of a 6.15″ pixel) over the 1.0 years of images: below the 0.7″/yr we can call real. As expected, the images show no significant motion (< 0.85″/yr). The fit gives 0.51 ± 0.17″/yr; a motion under 3 times its uncertainty, or under 0.7″/yr, is not claimed.

fitAnyway.floorText: floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 2 usable here)

expected.text: T Tauri star (young, varies irregularly). No fixed period.

tests.limit: Only images with no masked pixel within 15″ of the star count, each compared with first-season images from the same detector at the same wavelength: 64 of 120 images qualify (16 have a masked pixel within 15″ of the star; the rest have no first-season match). The catalogue gives no amplitude at these wavelengths, so only the fact of a change is tested. Control: on Barnard's Star, a steady star, the season averages stay within 0.05 mag of the first season (only 15 of its 120 images have no masked pixel within 15″).

measured.floorText: floor 0.15″/yr from field stars (all five fields; 0 usable here)

tests.limit: The catalogue motion (0.02″/yr) moves it only 0.031″ (0.005 of a 6.15″ pixel) over the 1.4 years of images: below the 0.7″/yr we can call real. The fit still finds 3.22 ± 1.03″/yr, which is not a real motion: the star carries the saturation flag in 119 of 120 images and its centre is blanked in 69 of the 69 fitted, so its position comes from the edges of a blanked core.
